Poppaea Sabina: Roman empress from 62 to 65 AD.

Founded in 1891 by Leandro N. Alem, this Argentine political party is the country's second-oldest active party and a longtime human-rights advocate that has been banned under military rule — which party?
Radical Civic Union: Political party in Argentina. The Radical Civic Union (Spanish: Unión Cívica Radical, UCR) is a major political party in Argentina.
Known by the abbreviation PRO and led by former Argentine president Mauricio Macri, which party has governed Buenos Aires since 2007?
Republican Proposal: Political party in Argentina.
This granddaughter of a Michigan governor chaired the Republican National Committee from 2017 until resigning in 2024, presiding over a string of election losses — who is she?
This Nazirite judge of ancient Israel slew a lion with his bare hands and later routed a Philistine army using only a donkey's jawbone — who was he?
Samson: Important character from the book of judges of the Hebrew Bible.
Born to a poor Cossack family and later a close ally of Stalin, this Soviet cavalry commander founded the Red Cavalry and became the subject of patriotic songs — who is he?
Only the second person to complete a full five-year term as Chief Minister of Karnataka, this Congress politician also served two stints as the state's Deputy Chief Minister — who is he?
Siddaramaiah: Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2013 to 2018 and 2023 to 2026.

On 26 September 1983, this Soviet duty officer judged his early-warning system's report of incoming U.S. missiles to be a false alarm — disobeying protocol and likely averting nuclear war. Who was he?
Stanislav Petrov: Soviet Air Defence Forces officer (1939–2017)

Running from 1912 to 1926 and named for its reigning emperor, this period in Japanese history saw political power shift from a group of elder statesmen to the country's parliamentary parties — what do historians call it?
Taishō era: Period of Japanese history from 1912 to 1926.
Serving as Lord Chancellor before becoming Archbishop of Canterbury, this cleric clashed with King Henry II and was murdered by the king's men in 1170 — who was he?
Thomas Becket: Archbishop of Canterbury from 1162 to 1170.
An economist who entered parliament via a 1981 by-election, this Samoan politician went on to serve as his country's prime minister from 1998 all the way to 2021 — who is he?
Tuilaʻepa Saʻilele Malielegaoi: Prime Minister of Samoa from 1998 to 2021. After Tofilau resigned in 1998, Tuilaʻepa became the prime minister and HRPP party leader.

Set to become just the fourth queen to rule her Scandinavian kingdom in her own right — and the first since 1720 — she is heir apparent thanks to a 1980 law that was Western Europe's first with absolute primogeniture. Who is she?
Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden: Heir apparent to the Swedish throne (born 1977)
Erupting in 1793 as a peasant revolt that turned Royalist, this French Revolutionary-era conflict was fought south of the Loire river and gave its combatants the nickname "Vendeans" — what was it?
War in the Vendée: 1793–1796 set of battles between the French revolutionaries and the royalists.
First built in the 11th century after the Norman conquest, this Berkshire royal residence has been used by the monarch since Henry I, making it the longest-occupied palace in Europe — which is it?
Windsor Castle: Official country residence of British monarch.
Made by young Indonesians on 28 October 1928, this nationalist declaration proclaimed one motherland, one nation, and one unifying language — what is it called?
Youth Pledge: 1928 declaration by Indonesian nationalists.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Haskell (founded 1990) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin is an astronomer. Despite completing her studies, because she was a woman Payne was not eligible to receive a degree from the University of Cambridge.
Who among these is a mathematician?
John Horton Conway is a mathematician. John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
In what year was Jane Goodall born?
Jane Goodall: Dame Valerie Jane Morris Goodall ( GUUD-awl; née Morris-Goodall; 3 April 1934 – 1 October 2025) was an English primatologist and anthropologist.
In what year was Jan Hus born?
Jan Hus: Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
In what year was Enrico Fermi born?
Enrico Fermi: With his colleagues, Fermi filed several patents related to the use of nuclear power, all of which were taken over by the US government.
In what year did Galileo Galilei die?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year did Paracelsus die?
Paracelsus also had a substantial influence as a prophet or diviner, his "Prognostications" being studied by Rosicrucians in the 17th century.
In what year was Tardigrade discovered?
Tardigrade: The earliest known fossil is from the Cambrian, some 500 million years ago.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
NASA X-43: Boeing. The NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Cannoli: Italy. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Who is credited with discovering Copernicium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Copernicium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
Who is credited with discovering Pluto?
Pluto: Clyde Tombaugh. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Who is credited with discovering Influenza A virus?
Influenza A virus: Christopher Andrewes. Influenza A virus, or IAV, is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
First flown in 1987, this medium-lift helicopter began as a joint UK-Italian venture between Westland and Agusta, and several countries use the nickname 'Merlin' for it — which helicopter is it?
AgustaWestland AW101 is a medium-lift helicopter in military and civil use.
In 1978, a run-in with a particle accelerator's proton beam left this Russian physicist with an extraordinary survival story after it passed straight through his head — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski (born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist.
This discipline studies past human activity by recovering and analyzing artifacts, architecture, and other material remains through surveying and excavation — name the field?
Archaeology is the study of human activity through the recovery and analysis of material culture.

These shelled marine crustaceans, cousins to crabs and lobsters, spend their adult lives cemented in place filtering food from the water — and folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety. What are they?
Barnacle are arthropods of the subclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea.
Known scientifically as Simuliidae, this family of small biting insects includes more than 2,200 named species, all but a handful belonging to a single genus — what are they commonly called?
Black fly (sometimes called buffalo gnats, turkey gnats, or white socks) are flies in the family Simuliidae of the Culicomorpha infraorder.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchi (large and medium-sized airways) in the lungs that causes coughing.
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
This woody perennial herb with bright blue flowers is cultivated for salad greens and a root that's roasted and ground as a coffee substitute. What plant is it?
Chicory (Cichorium intybus) is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.
This is the capacity to produce novel, valuable ideas or works — whether an invention, a scientific theory, a joke, or a piece of jewelry — through the exercise of imagination — what's the capacity?
Creativity is the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas or works through the exercise of imagination.

Distinguished from their one-leaved cousins by a pair of embryonic seed leaves, this classic angiosperm classification was shown by molecular science not to form a single evolutionary lineage — which plant group?
Dicotyledon (or, more rarely, dicotyls), are one of the two groups into which all the flowering plants (angiosperms) were formerly divided.
Born in German Pomerania and drawn by Franz Boas into documenting Native American languages, this anthropologist became a founding giant of American linguistics — who was he?

Edward Sapir (January 26, 1884 - February 4, 1939) was an American anthropologist-linguist, and one of the most important figures in the development of the discipline of linguistics in the United States.
This class of chemical compounds forms when the hydrogen of an acid's hydroxyl group is replaced by a carbon-based group, and includes the fatty-acid derivatives called glycerides. What is it?
Ester is a compound derived from an acid (either organic or inorganic) in which the hydrogen atom (H) of at least one acidic hydroxyl group (OH) of that acid is replaced by an organyl group (R).

With over 2,400 described species, these soft-bodied beetles produce light mainly at twilight, an ability that likely began as a larval warning signal before evolving into an adult mating display. Name this insect family?
Firefly are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.

Ranging from mild headaches and poor balance to severe confusion and seizures, this low-blood-sodium condition can be triggered by causes as varied as vomiting, diuretics, or overhydration — what's it called?
Hyponatremia is a low concentration of sodium in the blood. It is generally defined as a sodium concentration of less than 135 mmol/L (135 mEq/L), with severe hyponatremia being below 120 mEq/L.
Part of the fig and mulberry family and thriving in tropical lowlands, this giant of the produce world can weigh as much as 55 kg and measures up to 90 cm long — what is it?
Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is a species of tree in the fig, mulberry, and breadfruit family (Moraceae).
This Mexican-American astronaut flew on STS-128, led a branch at Johnson Space Center, and — urged on by President Obama — ran for Congress in 2012; who is he?
José M. Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, usually clearing up within two weeks. Name the condition?
Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (symbol Lv, number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — named for a California national laboratory. Which element is it?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Sometimes nicknamed 'sea cows,' these large, fully aquatic herbivorous marine mammals can grow up to 13 feet long and include Amazonian, West Indian, and West African species — what are they called?
Manatee (family Trichechidae, genus Trichechus) are large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammals sometimes known as sea cows.

This cluster of at least three conditions -- including high blood sugar, high triglycerides, and low 'good' cholesterol -- raises heart disease and diabetes risk in roughly a quarter of American adults. What is it called?

Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
Also called Indian mulberry, this tropical fruit tree contains harmful anthraquinones, and its foul-smelling fruit is mostly eaten only as a famine food — which species is it?
Morinda citrifolia is a fruit-bearing tree in the coffee family, Rubiaceae.
First linked by a Michigan doctor to farm wives sickened by isolation, this Gilded Age diagnosis grouped together fatigue, headaches, and a depressed mood — what condition?
Neurasthenia (from Ancient Greek (neuron) 'nerve' and (asthens) 'weak') is a term that was first used as early as 1829 for a mechanical weakness of the nerves.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Taking place over 24 hours at a large investment bank, this drama follows employees navigating the earliest hours of the 2008 financial crisis. What film is it?
Passerine is any bird of the order Passeriformes (from Latin passer 'sparrow' and formis '-shaped'), which includes more than half of all bird species.

Sitting at the intersection of textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly discipline studies language through oral and written historical sources — what is it called?
Philology (from Ancient Greek (philologa) 'love of word') is the study of language in oral and written historical sources.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.
What dimensionless quantity in fluid dynamics, expressing the ratio of inertial to viscous forces, determines whether a flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent?
Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity that helps predict fluid flow patterns in different situations by measuring the ratio between inertial and viscous forces.
Named after an American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, gram-negative bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes within a single major species — name it?
Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.
This Pakistani-American businessman owns both an NFL franchise, the Jacksonville Jaguars, and an English Premier League club, Fulham — who is he?
Shahid Khan (born July 18, 1950) is a Pakistani and American businessman.
The largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator alive, this pelagic giant has females who give birth only every four to twenty years — what is it?
Sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) is the largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator.

Which British single-seat fighter plane, the only such aircraft Britain produced continuously throughout World War II, was famous for its innovative elliptical wing designed to be as thin as possible?
Supermarine Spitfire is a British single-seat fighter aircraft that was used by the Royal Air Force and other Allied countries before, during, and after World War II.
Used to treat asthma and COPD, this methylxanthine drug — a cousin of caffeine — turns up in trace amounts in tea, chocolate, and yerba mate. What is it?
Theophylline is a drug that inhibits phosphodiesterase and blocks adenosine receptors.
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Known also as sight or eyesight, this sense lets the body detect photons and build a picture of its environment using daytime or night modes — what is it?
Visual perception is the ability to detect light and use it to form an image of the surrounding environment.
Known for a rapid side-to-side flight just before landing and living only in colonies, these black-and-yellow social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula go by what North American name?
Yellowjacket is the common name in North America for predatory social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula.
A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Formed when hydrogen atoms in ammonia are swapped out for carbon-based groups, which class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds includes aniline as its simplest aromatic member?
Amine: Chemical compounds and groups containing nitrogen with a lone pair (:N)

A German pharmacist coined this pigment's name from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue' in 1835 — it shifts red to purple to blue depending on pH and colors blueberries, black rice, and autumn leaves; what is it?
Native to eastern North America's wet woods and swamps, this shrub genus produces bitter 'chokeberries' that reached Scandinavia and Russia by the eighteenth century — what genus is this?

Aronia: Genus of plants (chokeberries). Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy,' which term denotes a statement accepted as true without proof, serving as a starting point for further reasoning?
Axiom: Statement that is taken to be true.
This common, noncancerous enlargement of a male gland can cause frequent urination and a weak stream; it isn't linked to poor hygiene, and there's no known cure. What's the condition?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia: Noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
Composed of plasma plus red cells, white cells, and platelets, this circulatory fluid delivers oxygen and nutrients to the body while carrying away waste — what is it?
Blood: Body fluid in the circulatory system. Plasma, which constitutes 55% of blood fluid, is mostly water (92% by volume), and contains proteins, glucose, mineral ions, and hormones.
This plant family — nicknamed the mustards or crucifers, and including cabbage — hosts the caterpillars of a notorious garden-pest butterfly as one of its worst enemies — name the family?

Ranging from the hefty black species of the Amazon basin to the diminutive dwarf species just over a metre long, these Central and South American relatives of alligators make up their own reptile subfamily — what are they called?
Caiman: Subfamily of reptiles. The black caiman is the largest caiman species in the world and is found in the slow-moving rivers and lakes that surround the Amazon basin.

Born in London, raised in Milan, and self-taught in web design, this Catholic teenager built a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles before dying of leukemia at fifteen — he was beatified in 2020. Who was he?
Which second-generation antihistamine for hay fever kicks in within half an hour but is more likely than fexofenadine or loratadine to cause drowsiness?

Cetirizine: Antihistamine medication. Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
This plant genus includes both chicory, whose roasted roots make a coffee substitute, and true endive, the base for salad greens like escarole — which genus?
Cichorium: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.

Believed to be the first coffee species ever cultivated, this plant, native to the forests of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen, still accounts for roughly 60% of global coffee production — what's its scientific name?
Coffea arabica: Species of coffee plant. Coffea arabica, also known as the Arabica coffee, is a species of flowering plant in the coffee and madder family Rubiaceae.
Found only in placental mammals, this roughly four-inch bundle of 200 to 300 million nerve fibers is the brain's largest white-matter structure, linking its left and right hemispheres — what is it?
Corpus callosum: White matter tract connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.
Inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, this disorder coats the lungs and other organs in thick mucus, inviting repeated bacterial infections — what genetic condition is it?
Cystic fibrosis: Genetic disorder affecting mostly the lungs.

Doctors once spotted this endocrine condition by its three Ps — polydipsia, polyuria, and polyphagia, or excessive thirst, urination, and hunger — all tracing back to trouble with insulin. Which disease is it?
Diabetes: Group of endocrine diseases characterized by high blood sugar levels.

Aristotle's Poetics contrasted this performance-based mode with the epic and the lyrical, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning "deed" or "act" — the two-masks symbol marks its split into comedy and tragedy. What is it?
Drama: Artwork intended for performance; formal type of literature.
Named for the large trunk-like proboscis of its males, this giant oceangoing pinniped can weigh up to 4,000 kilograms and was once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil. What animal is it?
Elephant seal: Genus of aquatic carnivores.
Sold under the brand name Nexium, this proton pump inhibitor treats acid reflux by blocking an enzyme in the stomach's acid-producing cells — what is it?
Esomeprazole: Medication which reduces stomach acid.
While its deciduous neighbors drop everything and go bare for winter, this kind of plant keeps its foliage green and working all year round — what's the botanical term?
Evergreen: Plant that has leaves in all seasons.
This beetle family produces light mainly at twilight to attract mates — though some females mimic another species' flash pattern just to lure and eat the males — what are they commonly called?
Firefly: Family of beetles. The Lampyridae are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
A French economist who gave up accounting to lecture across France, he founded peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union before sharing the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901. Who was he?
Frédéric Passy: French economist and pacifist (1822–1912)

Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater wields a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth, and the males sport a bulbous, pot-shaped bump on the tip that gives the animal its name. What is it?
Gharial: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent.
The seeds of five plants in this family, including rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane, cover 46% of the world's farmland — what group of plants is this?
Grass: Collective name for three families of plants.
This British mathematician has studied the math of dating and pandemics, delivered the Royal Institution's 2019 Christmas Lectures, and hosted BBC's 'Secret Genius of Modern Life' — who is she?
Hannah Fry: British mathematician and broadcaster (born 1984)
Its name Greek for 'different wings,' this insect suborder of about 40,000 species is the group most consistently termed 'true bugs' within Hemiptera — which group is it?
Heteroptera: Suborder of true bugs. The name "Heteroptera" is used in two very different ways in modern classifications.
Also known as dihydrocodeinone, this semi-synthetic opioid is often combined with acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain and is sold alone as an extended-release drug called Zohydro ER — what is it?
Hydrocodone: Opioid drug used in pain relief.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.

This Scottish physicist's equations unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single theory — the second great unification in physics after Newton's — while also helping found statistical mechanics — who is he?
James Clerk Maxwell: Scottish physicist and mathematician (1831–1879)
Nicknamed 'Father of the National Parks,' this Scottish-born naturalist co-founded the Sierra Club and helped preserve Yosemite Valley and Sequoia National Park — who is he?
Nicknamed the 'honey bear' though unrelated to actual bears, this nocturnal rainforest mammal is the only member of its genus and a cousin of raccoons and coatis — which arboreal creature?
This biennial vegetable in the onion family has an edible bundle of leaf sheaths sometimes colloquially called a 'stem' — what is it?
Leek: Vegetable in the onion family. A leek is a biennial vegetable, a cultivar of Allium ampeloprasum, the broadleaf wild leek (syn.
Tucked mostly beneath the right rib cage, this organ detoxifies the body, stores glucose as glycogen, and produces the bile that helps digest fat — which organ?
Liver: Vertebrate organ involved in metabolism.
First synthesized in 1912 by a Merck chemist, this stimulant known on the street as ecstasy or molly became linked to raves and electronic dance music in the 1980s — which drug?
MDMA: Psychoactive drug, often called ecstasy.
Known by the pseudonym 'Notch,' this Swedish programmer created the best-selling video game of all time and became a billionaire when Microsoft bought his studio for $2.5 billion in 2014 — who is he?
Markus Persson: Swedish video game programmer (born 1979)
This rose-family shrub, commonly known as the medlar, produces fruit that's traditionally eaten only after it has softened past ripeness — what's its scientific name?
Mespilus germanica: Fruit tree, the medlar. Mespilus germanica, known as the medlar or common medlar, is a large shrub or small tree in the rose family Rosaceae.
Produced by mammary glands and rich in calcium, protein and lactose, this liquid is often prized for its antibody-packed early form, colostrum — what is it?
Milk: Nutrient-rich liquid produced by mammals.
Grown above the upper lip and below the nose, this facial hair style has taken many forms across history — what is it called?
Moustache: Strip of facial hair across the upper lip. A moustache (UK:) or mustache (US:) is a growth of facial hair grown above the upper lip and under the nose of men.

Attributed to 19th-century pathologist Rudolf Virchow, this term for the premature death of cells caused by trauma or infection contrasts with the body's own programmed cell death — what's the condition called?
Necrosis: Unprogrammed cell death caused by external cell injury.
Introduced to Hawaii in 1929, this crested songbird serves as the state bird of seven US states including Ohio and Virginia — which bird?
Northern cardinal: Species of North American bird.
Found on every continent but Antarctica, these flowers can lure pollinators by mimicking female insects, and their tiny seeds depend on fungal partners just to sprout. What plant family is this?
Orchid: Family of flowering plants in the order Asparagales.
Secreted by small neck glands when blood calcium runs low, this peptide messenger raises calcium levels and boosts active vitamin D production — which one?
Parathyroid hormone: Mammalian protein found in humans.
Created by Larry Wall in 1987 as a Unix scripting tool for report processing, this language's planned sixth version was eventually spun off and renamed Raku — which programming language?
Perl: Interpreted programming language first released in 1987.
Domesticated twice in the Neolithic — once near the Tigris Basin and once in China — this even-toed, hoofed omnivore is farmed mainly for pork; what is it?

In this group of disorders, pigment-like substances called porphyrins accumulate in the body, triggering attacks of abdominal pain, confusion, and even seizures that can be set off by alcohol or fasting. What is it?
Porphyria: Metabolic disorders in which porphyrins build up in the body.
Nicknamed the 'liberty cap' for its distinctive conical shape, this psychoactive mushroom grows in grassland and produces psilocybin — what is it?
Psilocybe semilanceata: Species of fungus in the family Hymenogastraceae, native to Europe.
This Indian social activist founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan and later teamed with yoga guru Ramdev to promote swadeshi economics — who was he?
Rajiv Dixit: Indian activist. Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 – 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.
Holding Oxford's inaugural chair for the Public Understanding of Science, which outspoken atheist and evolutionary biologist wrote 'The Selfish Gene'?
Richard Dawkins: British evolutionary biologist and author (born 1941)
This extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period had closely-spaced eyes at the front of its head, 'like car headlamps,' and is best known from fossils found in Bolivia — what is it?
Sacabambaspis: Extinct genus of jawless fishes.
Distinguished from true seals by external ear flaps and the ability to walk on all fours, these marine mammals include a giant subspecies that can weigh up to 1,000 kilograms. What are they?
Sea lion: Subfamily of aquatic mammals.

Composed of repeating siloxane units with a backbone of oxygen and silicon rather than carbon, this synthetic material fills sealants, cookware, and medical devices, and is often confused with the chip-making element it's named after — what is it?

Introduced in Einstein's 1905 paper 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies,' this theory rests on two postulates — that physical laws hold in every non-accelerating frame, and that light's speed is constant for all observers. What is it called?
Special relativity: Theory of interwoven space and time by Albert Einstein.

Caused by blocked or bleeding blood flow to the brain, this medical emergency can cause facial drooping and one-sided weakness — and if symptoms fade within a day, it's called a 'mini' version instead. What is this condition?
Stroke: Death of a region of brain cells due to poor blood flow.
Turkey's only female prime minister to date, this economist-turned-politician led the country from 1993 to 1996 as head of the True Path Party — who is she?
Tansu Çiller: Prime Minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996. As a professor of economics, Çiller was appointed Minister of State for the economy by Prime Minister Süleyman Demirel in 1991.

Grain processing strips so much of this micronutrient that many countries enrich their flours to replace it; a deficiency leads to beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy. Also known as vitamin B1, which essential nutrient is it?
Thiamine: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.
Linked to the use of highly absorbent tampons, this bacterial-toxin condition causes fever, rash, skin peeling, and a dangerous drop in blood pressure — which condition?
